prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases such as cereblon to direct proteins to destruction, from the first PROTACs to the molecular-glue mechanism of thalidomide-class drugs

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration from photoredox catalysis (B064) to targeted protein degradation (B044) with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. My round-1 objection was structural: I doubted that degrader-bound ternary complexes were numerous enough to support design rules. On reflection the committee case does not rest on a catalogue of ternary structures. It rests on two points. First, the cereblon-thalidomide mechanism was established by identification of the target and by crystal structures of the cereblon-DDB1 assembly with the drug, so the molecular-glue half has real structural evidence. Second, the PROTAC half has been reproduced across many laboratories, ligases and targets, and structure-guided work on degrader-bound complexes has shown that cooperativity is something one can measure and design, even if the rules are not yet general. The principle is simple and chemical: a small molecule induces proximity between a ligase and a target, and the pharmacology becomes event-driven. It reaches proteins with no active site, it has opened a new field, and every member has listed it somewhere. Crews and Deshaies conceived the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon and anchors the glue branch, which a single citation can name without implying that cereblon work is PROTAC chemistry.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved to my knowledge (unverified), so patient benefit is still prospective, and the committee could fairly wait. The citation joins two lines with different origins, and a three-person cap omits Ciulli, whose structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work I value, as well as Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim. Handa's contribution is target identification, and Somfai's question about what was new chemically is a fair one. My former choice, photoredox catalysis, is the more mature and chemically transparent toolbox, but it has no support from other members, crowded priority among MacMillan, Yoon, Stephenson, Fukuzumi, Konig, Nicewicz and Melchiorre, and the repeat-recognition problem for MacMillan.

responses.point: Degradation is a programmable chemical event with a clear design rule, the cereblon discovery gives the glue branch a mechanistic explanation, and the mechanism is established whether or not a drug is approved.
responses.response: I ranked this eighth, and my two objections were ternary-complex structure and the missing approval. You answered the second in a way I accept: the mechanism has been independently reproduced, and approval would test usefulness, not whether the chemistry is real. On the first, I now weigh the cereblon-drug structures and the measured cooperativity more heavily than the count of degrader-bound complexes, so I withdraw that objection as a reason for exclusion. I still agree with your own point that PROTAC design and the glue mechanism may be two achievements. I would accept your citation wording, which names cereblon and so keeps the glue branch tied to evidence.

responses.point: A three-person configuration of Crews, Deshaies and Handa with one unifying citation is defensible, and Handa is preferred to Ciulli because the molecular-glue half is hard to defend without cereblon.
responses.response: I agree with the change from Ciulli to Handa and arrive at it for a structural reason. The thalidomide-cereblon result is the one place where a drug mechanism was settled by identifying the protein target and then by crystal structures of the complex, which is the standard of evidence I apply. Ciulli's VHL work is excellent and I would give him real weight if the committee limited the prize to PROTAC design, but then the citation would drop the glue branch you cite as a reason for the single achievement. I share your unease about stapling two discoveries together. The citation I propose uses the shared principle of directing proteins to a ubiquitin ligase and names cereblon explicitly, so it does not claim Handa did PROTAC chemistry.

responses.point: A two-part prize of base editing for Liu alone and degradation for Crews and Deshaies, with Handa omitted unless the committee prefers a single achievement.
responses.response: I do not support B019 in my configuration. The deaminase chemistry is explicit, but Liu as sole credit is contested by five members, Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida all have claims, and prime editing complicates the framing. A Cas9-based platform also sits close to the 2020 prize. On Handa, you said you would accept him as the third name if the committee prefers a single achievement. I think it should, because without cereblon the citation has no mechanistic account of thalidomide-class glues, which is the part of the field with the longest and best-documented structural basis. A Crews-and-Deshaies-only prize would be cleaner on credit but narrower.

responses.point: Nitrogenase is attributable, mature and important, with structure established by crystallography over three decades and a physically explicit mechanism, for Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt.
responses.response: I keep nitrogenase as a serious alternative, and I agree the cofactor structure with its interstitial carbide is the best-established result on the shortlist. What stops me from preferring it is the same point you concede: the E4 state, substrate-binding site and order of proton and electron delivery are unsettled, so a citation that says 'catalytic mechanism' overstates what is known. If the committee went there I would want the citation limited to structure and function of the cofactor, and I would still want Dean's genetics and biosynthesis work weighed against Seefeldt. I do not see that it can draw more votes than degradation, so I am not advancing it as my first choice.

responses.point: Buchwald-Hartwig C-N coupling has the cleanest two-person attribution and mechanistic detail, but overlaps with the 2010 cross-coupling prize; photoredox is your closest alternative with an allocation problem.
responses.response: You are right that the allocation problem in photoredox is harder than any doubt about its importance, and your point on the MacMillan repeat is why I am leaving B064 as an alternative. On C-N coupling, I still see it as a mature reaction class that was extended from an honoured concept, and it has no support from other members, so I cannot answer your novelty question in its favour. On the cereblon discovery, I agree it is chiefly target identification, but it is also what explained why thalidomide acts, and it supplied the structural basis for a new mode of drug action. I take your question about what was new chemically seriously and still judge that the induced-proximity principle qualifies.

uncertainties: Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug, which I could not verify, will cause other members to judge the prize premature.
Whether one citation can unify PROTACs and cereblon-based glues without implying that Handa's contribution is PROTAC design, and whether Ciulli deserves the third place instead.
Whether photoredox could draw any support if degradation fails, given the MacMillan repeat issue and the crowded priority claims.
Whether the nitrogenase mechanism will be settled enough to support a citation beyond the cofactor structure.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, who prefers nitrogenase (B032), which I list only as an alternative; I have no collaboration with any credited person on the shortlist. My own work on 3D electron diffraction is not part of any shortlisted candidate, and my change of position was reached from the round-1 exchange and not from any collegial tie.
